transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess things just got a little out of hand at work recently. 

I do landscaping, and normally I'm just a regular crew guy, you know? Just keeping my head down and doing my job. But... well, lately I got really, really motivated. Maybe a bit too much, if that makes sense? I went from just doing my normal work to suddenly trying to run three different bids at the same time. I was calling city people, lining up all these plant suppliers, and just messaging absolutely everybody I knew about this huge park idea I had. 

I mean, I thought I was just being really productive and helping out the company, but it got to the point where it was like I just couldn't shut it off. It was a bit much, I guess. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up... does that sound like the kind of thing you can help with?
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or unusually irritable where this kind of behavior came naturally and easily to you?

Um, yeah, I guess you could say that. I mean, I wouldn't say I was out of control or anything, just... really, really fired up. It felt good, honestly. Like I was, I don't know, almost bigger than myself, if that makes sense? I was just so focused on getting everything done. 

But, um... I guess maybe I did get a little... short with people. Like, if one of the guys on the crew asked why I was doing so much, or told me to maybe take a break and slow down... I kind of snapped at them. Probably a lot harder than I should have. I feel really bad about it now, because they were just trying to help, and I know I overreacted. I'm not usually like that, I swear. I try to get along with everyone. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a total jerk.
Can you tell me if this feeling of being really fired up and energetic lasted for at least several days without letting up, or did it come and go more quickly?

Um, it didn't really come and go, no. It stuck around for a while. I hope that's normal? 

It started right around when I decided to, um, kind of remake my whole image for that big park pitch I mentioned. I just felt so clear-headed and ready to tackle the world, you know? And that whole... fired-up, overconfident feeling, it lasted for about two weeks straight. It was just go, go, go the whole time. 

And then... well, then I just kind of crashed. Really hard. But for those two weeks, it was pretty constant. Is that the kind of timeline you usually hear about from people? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if during that two-week period, you felt your mood was elevated, expansive, or unusually irritable most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, yeah, I'd say so. Like I said, for those two weeks before I crashed, I just felt... really fired up. It was most of the day, pretty much every day. I felt great, honestly, like I was almost bigger than myself and could handle anything. 

But, um... yeah, the irritable part was there too. Like I mentioned, if one of my coworkers questioned my plan or told me I needed to slow down, I'd just... I'd snap at him. Way harder than made sense, looking back on it. I feel terrible about it because I really try to be easy to work with. I hope that doesn't make me sound too awful? I just... I couldn't seem to help it during those couple of weeks. Is that... is that helpful for you to know?
Can you tell me if this mood you described — being really fired up and irritable — was noticeably different from your usual self, or is this just how you typically are most of the time?

Um, no, it was definitely different. I mean, I'm usually a pretty laid-back guy, you know? I like to keep my head down, do my work, and get along with the crew. I'm not the kind of person who goes around snapping at people or acting like I own the place. 

So, yeah, those two weeks... it was like I was a different person, almost. Just way more intense than I usually am. I hope that's okay to say? I just really want to make sure you know that I'm not normally that... difficult to be around. I try really hard to be a good guy. Does that make sense?

Can you tell me if, during those two weeks, you felt that your activity level was significantly increased — like you were driven to keep going or had an inner sense of restlessness that you couldn’t shut off?

Um, yeah, I guess you could say that. I mean, I've always been a hard worker, you know? In landscaping, you kind of have to be. But... yeah, during those two weeks, it was definitely kicked into overdrive. 

I was, um, I was getting up way before daylight. I'd be out there loading up the tools, sketching out new flower beds, pricing out all these native plants I wanted to use for the park pitch. And the thing is, even after working a full day outside—which usually wipes a guy out—I just... I felt like I had to keep going. Like I couldn't just sit down and relax. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound frantic or anything? I was getting a lot done, which I thought was a good thing at the time. I just really wanted to impress the bosses. Is it normal to have that much energy when you're just really motivated about a project? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

During those two weeks when you felt so fired up and were working non-stop, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual — like you could get by on just a few hours of sleep or didn't feel tired even if you didn’t sleep much?

Um, well... I guess I didn't sleep a whole lot during that time. But, you know, I think a lot of guys in my line of work just power through when there's a big job, right? 

I was probably getting maybe three or four hours a night. But I honestly didn't feel that tired! I felt pretty good, actually. I mean, I'd wake up at 3 AM and just feel totally ready to tackle the day. I didn't feel groggy or anything like I usually do if I miss sleep. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I was being irresponsible with my health or anything. I just... I had all these ideas for the project and I didn't want to lose momentum, you know? I really wanted to do a good job. Is it okay that I was functioning on that little sleep, since I felt fine? I mean, I wasn't falling asleep on the mower or anything dangerous like that.
During those two weeks when you felt so fired up and productive, did you feel like you had special abilities, were more important than usual, or could accomplish things that most people couldn’t?

Um, well... I guess I did feel pretty confident. I mean, maybe a little more than usual? I don't want to sound arrogant or anything, because I really try to stay humble. But, yeah, during that time... I kind of got it in my head that I was going to be, like, the top guy in the area. 

I honestly believed I was about to become the guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. Like I had this special vision for it that nobody else did. Which, looking back, is a little embarrassing to admit, because, you know, I'm really just trying to keep my small, regular jobs paid up right now. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I have a big ego? I just really believed in the work I was doing and thought it was going to change everything for me. Is it normal to get a little carried away with your own ideas when you're that passionate about a project? I just want to make sure you know I don't usually walk around thinking I'm better than everybody else.
Did what you experienced during that time cause any serious problems in your life — like issues at work, trouble with relationships, or anything that made it hard to function normally?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it caused any *serious* problems. I mean, I definitely didn't get into any fights or, you know, blow up my life or anything. I try really hard to be professional. 

But... I guess maybe it did make things a little harder than I realized at the time. Like, because I was moving so fast and trying to do so much, I... I kind of started missing some details. Just small things, mostly! But, um, like missing a measurement here or leaving something off a bid. 

I'm really trying to be careful now, though, because I'm just so worried that one bad mistake could cost me clients, or worse, get someone hurt on a job site with the equipment. I don't want you to think I'm careless with my work—I really do take safety seriously. Is it pretty common for people to make a few little mistakes when they're rushing because they're so excited about a project? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Just to clarify, you mentioned the time period lasted about two weeks. Would you say that the entire time — all 14 days — you felt that way without a break, or were there any full days where you felt more like your usual self?

Um, well... yeah, it was pretty much the whole two weeks. I mean, I really hope I'm remembering it right, but... yeah, from the day I started trying to, you know, completely remake myself for that big park pitch, it just didn't stop. 

I was just going and going for those full two weeks, right up until I just... kind of crashed. There wasn't really a day where I felt like regular old me. I was just so focused on the pitch. 

I hope it's okay that it lasted that long? I mean, I wasn't trying to push myself too hard, it just sort of happened that way. Is it normal to get stuck in that kind of... overdrive... for a couple of weeks straight when you're working on something important? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Can you tell me if, after those two weeks when you crashed, you felt extremely down, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had trouble functioning normally for a period of time?

Um, yeah... I definitely felt down after that. I mean, honestly, I've been feeling pretty down for... well, about a year now, off and on. I really try not to let it show, because I want to be someone people can rely on, you know? I don't want to be a burden or seem lazy. 

But this latest crash... after those two weeks, it's just been really, really hard. Probably the worst it's been. It's like I just can't find the energy to care about the things I normally like doing. I still try to get up and do my job, but it takes everything I have just to get through the day. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound weak. I'm really trying my best to push through it. Is it pretty common for people to have a really bad dip like that after working so hard on something? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right, so you have all the pieces.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presented with a distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, and irritable mood lasting at least 4 days (clearly observed to last 2 weeks), accompanied by increased goal-directed activity, decreased need for sleep, and inflated self-esteem. This manic episode is not better explained by another condition and caused mild functional impairment. There is also evidence of a subsequent depressive episode, but the presence of mania confirms bipolar I disorder.
